text:
I would like to clarify something from the side of האגודה הישראלית לזוגות בינלאומיים aic.org.il, which is the nonprofit organization that represents this community. 
As a registered nonprofit in Israel, we are prevented from engaging in political activity, or endorsing any party or candidate politically. 
However, we encourage everyone in this group to educate themselves about politics in Israel and how it affects them. We encourage you to read our reports about AIC's parliamentary activity and understand the political agendas around immigration, and make educated decisions based on that:
https://aic.org.il/tag/knesset/

Regarding being a strong lobby inside a certain party - I actually don't think our community is too small. With around 40,000 Israelis in an active process (and thousands who completed it) that's definitely enough to make a difference. Our problem is different - we are not organized or united. We are coming from different backgrounds, mostly with very low political awareness. The hardships usually end after 5-8 years, and then people forget about it and move on with their lives. For this reason, the number of people who actually care about making a difference is lower than you think (I know this based on AIC donation stats, and you can also see this in our number of followers across platforms).

Building a strong lobby inside a party takes years and a dedicated community, I don't think we have either of those unfortunately
